newsitem.title: USA: New York State gets extension on Food Stamps-paper.
newsitem.headline: New York State gets extension on Food Stamps-paper.

text.p: New York State got a five-month reprieve from the Clinton Administration that will allow local governments to continue Food Stamp benefits for legal immigrants, the New York Times reported Wednesday.

Food Stamps are paid for by the federal government, so the state incurred no costs in making the request, which will let from 150,000 to 250,000 legal immingrants collect benefits through Aug 22, the paper said.

Aides to Gov. George Pataki told the Times that he was extending the benefits in the hope that Congress and President Bill Clinton would soften some of the harsher aspects of the welfare law enacted last August.
State officials also said the extension would give immigrants more time to apply for an exemption that would allow some to keep their benefits permanently.
